title: Katechon Technology
description: Katechon Technology visual explainer for Dune Ventures.

slides.headline:
Pages ->
Channels
slides.narration: The framing is simple: the internet container is changing. Pages were fixed documents. Feeds were streams of posts. Channels are live software objects that people can watch, talk to, and reshape.

slides.headline:
Agent + I/O
+ Surface
slides.narration: A Katechon channel is not a video channel. It is a live software object: inputs, outputs, a specialist agent, memory, state, and a surface that can change.

slides.headline:
Kat routes
expertise.
slides.narration: Kat is the face and continuity layer. Underneath, specialist agents do the actual channel work: markets, OSINT, news, science, infrastructure, and anything else the user opens.

slides.headline:
The surface
changes.
slides.narration: Mutable is the key unlock. The user does not adapt to the dashboard. The channel adapts to the user: focus, data, layout, surfaces, and next actions all move together.

slides.headline:
Surface, not
destination.
slides.narration: A dashboard becomes a surface. The stage can be replaced, the rail can explain context, and action blocks can appear without losing the channel's state.

slides.headline:
One turn ->
new state
slides.narration: Every meaningful turn becomes a state transition. The runtime parses intent, updates channel state, queries data, chooses a layout, replaces surfaces, and tells the user what changed.

slides.headline: BTC / 3M
slides.narration: For example: BTC over three months. The crypto channel turns that phrase into a real investigation: it queries data, renders history, labels provenance, and offers the next useful moves.

slides.headline:
Useful states,
not links.
slides.narration: This is the future Katechon is building toward. Discovery stops being only links to pages or videos. It becomes routing people into useful live software states: things they watch, modify, command, and act inside.
